examples: The baby is asleep.
A baby smiled at me.
The baby drinks milk.

more.def: A very young child, or the young of an animal.
examples: The baby giggled when I made a silly face.
A baby elephant stays close to its mother.
My cousin just had a baby.
I came back home.
Please give it back.
She went back to bed.

more.def: To a place or condition where someone or something was earlier.
examples: After the picnic, we walked back to the car.
He gave the library book back on Monday.
The tide goes out and then comes back in.

easy.def: The part of your body behind you, between your neck and your legs.
examples: My back hurts.
The cat has a soft back.
She carried me on her back.

more.def: The part of the body on the opposite side from the front, or the rear part of something.
examples: The turtle pulled its head into its shell on its back.
We sat in the back of the bus.
He scratched the dog's back with a brush.
The milk smells bad.
That was a bad dream.
It is bad weather.

more.def: Not good, or causing harm or trouble.
examples: The bad weather kept us inside all weekend.
Eating too much candy is bad for your teeth.
He had a bad cold and stayed home from school.

easy.def: A soft holder for carrying things.
examples: Put your lunch in the bag.
My bag is heavy.
Mom has a bag of apples.

more.def: A container made of paper, plastic or cloth for carrying or holding things.
examples: She packed her swimsuit in a bag.
We filled three bags with leaves.
A bag of flour sat on the shelf.

easy.def: To stay up and not fall over.
examples: I can balance on one foot.
The seal balances a ball on its nose.
Can you balance a book on your head?

more.def: To keep yourself or an object steady so it does not tip or fall.
examples: The gymnast balanced on the narrow beam without wobbling.
He balanced the tray of drinks as he walked across the room.
It is hard to balance on a bike when you first learn to ride.
Throw the ball.
The dog chased the ball.
We kick the ball.

more.def: A round object used in games and sports.
examples: He threw the ball over the fence.
A basketball is a large orange ball.
The kitten batted a ball of yarn across the floor.

easy.def: A long, hard piece of something.
examples: A bar of soap.
He ate a granola bar.
A metal bar.

more.def: A long, straight piece of something hard.
examples: A metal bar held the gate shut.
She washed her hands with a bar of soap.
He ate a granola bar for a snack.

easy.def: A small animal that flies at night.
examples: A bat flew out of the cave.
Bats sleep in the day.
We saw a bat in the barn.

more.def: A small furry animal with wings that sleeps in the day and flies at night.
examples: The bat hung upside down from the roof of the cave.
A bat can eat hundreds of insects in one night.
Bats use sound to find their way in the dark.

easy.def: A stick you use to hit a ball.
examples: She hit the ball with her bat.
My bat is made of wood.
He left his bat at the park.

more.def: A wooden or metal stick used to hit the ball in games like baseball and cricket.
examples: He swung the bat and sent the ball over the fence.
The coach handed each player a helmet and a bat.
Her new bat is lighter than her old one.

easy.def: To hit something, like a ball.
examples: The cat likes to bat the toy.
It is my turn to bat.
The baby bats at the toy over her crib.

more.def: To hit at something with a bat or with your hand or paw.
examples: The kitten batted the string back and forth.
Our best hitter will bat first in the next game.
She batted the balloon up into the air.
